slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Draw a circle. Keeping the same compass opening, put the needle anywhere on the circle and draw another circle. Move the needle to where the new circle crosses the first, and repeat around. The six circles meet at the center and at six equally spaced points: the six-petal rosette.

The radius used as a chord subtends a 60-degree central angle, so six such chords close a regular hexagon. The circumference is 2π radii, not six. At this point label the 60-degree explanation a preview, proved after Unit 5. Preview, proved after Unit 5: each petal tip, its neighbor and the center form an equilateral triangle.
